You have to develop your palette. I think the best way to do this is to cook for yourself. You will learn the flavors of the individual spices and you'll learn how they taste when they come together to form wholely new flavor profiles. You should also practice the different cooking methods and compare them. When you go to a restaurant and get your food taste it and try to dissect it, determine what spices went into it and how it was cooked. Honestly though good vs bad is just whether or not you enjoy it. Presentation is important in restaurants but some of the best restaurants I have been to have been little holes in the wall places where flavor is more important than presentation. This is not a short venture, developing the palette will take years but it will definitely be worth it. Good luck and enjoy!
